column8:
Monitor:
- Monitor the forecast for heatwave: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/specialised-forecasts-and-observations/heatwave
Mitigation:
- Do pre-start checks on engine coolant, hydraulics and electrical components. Park cranes and vehicles in shade. Shade temperature-sensitive equipment (e.g. with tarpaulin). Use reflective insulation in crane cabins.
- Store materials in shade. Wear suitable gloves and PPE.
- Provide cool drinking water. Brief workers on heat-illness signs.
- Check that alarms and temperature monitoring are working.
column9:
Monitor:
- Monitor the forecast for heatwave: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/specialised-forecasts-and-observations/heatwave
- Monitor temperatures continuously. Brief the crew daily on current and next-day conditions.
Mitigation:
- Move high-load and heat-intensive work to early morning or night. Add mid-shift checks of coolant, hydraulic and electrical components. Cover or shade all sensitive equipment.
- Allow hot materials and equipment to cool before handling. Use mechanical aids (forklift, hoist, vacuum lifters) for heavy or hot items.
- Increase rest breaks in cool, shaded areas. Improve ventilation or air conditioning, and use outdoor misting fans for outdoor work. Supervisors monitor workers for symptoms.
column10:
Monitor:
- Monitor the forecast for heatwave: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/specialised-forecasts-and-observations/heatwave
Mitigation:
- Restrict high-load and heat-intensive operations to cooler periods only, or defer them. Stop any equipment that exceeds manufacturer limits. Allow a cool-down period before restart.
- Handle hot materials only with mechanical aids. Defer non-essential handling and lifting to cooler periods.
- Apply a buddy system and frequent symptom checks. Take longer or more frequent rest breaks. Reschedule outdoor work to the coolest period, or stop it.
- Stop operation when the temperature limit is exceeded, then apply a cool-down period. Decide to resume only after review by the supervisor or site manager.

column8:
Monitor:
- Inspect erosion and sediment controls (ESCs) at standard minimum,e.g. weekly, before shutdown periods, and after rainfall that generates runoff
- Erosion warning indicator can be found on: https://mapshare.vic.gov.au/coastkit/
- Check coastal hazard warning:
https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
https://www.emergency.vic.gov.au/respond/#
- Record erosion warning indicator (EWI) and inspection actions in Intelex system (or equivalent)
Mitigation:
- Use erosion control blanket on disturbed open sediment.
- Install silt fence to contain coarse sediment while letting the water pass.
- Check ESC materials are stocked on-site.
- Repair or desilt ESCs when capacity falls by 40%, and desilt to keep at least 70% sediment storage capacity. Complete repairs before the next rainfall event
- Check any discharge against the standard: TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, pH 6.5-8.5, no visible oil or grease (Section 8.0).
Communication:
- The Site Environmental Advisor and supervisor record the trigger and brief the crew if there is escalation
column9:
Monitor:
- Increase monitoring, inspect daily and after every runoff-generating rainfall event
- Mark and survey the affected areas, compare recession against the historical averages
- Record inspections, erosion warning indicator can be found on: https://mapshare.vic.gov.au/coastkit/
- Check coastal hazard warning:
https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
https://www.emergency.vic.gov.au/respond/#
Mitigation:
- Continue T1 controls and extend blanket and silt fence coverage to all active erosion areas. Apply permeating grouting to areas showing active erosion.
- Repair as T1, with repairs completed within 24 hours or before forecast rain
- Add receiving-water monitoring at appropriate intervals. Check that grouting products do not affect the surrounded water quality (check the total suspended solid (TSS) and total dissolved solid (TDS))
Communication:
- Notify PIC and construction manager when T2 is triggered
- Environmental advisor review and update the Erosion and Sediment Control Plan (ESCP) if needed
column10:
Monitor:
- Multiple daily inspections of the affected area. Survey the extent and rate of erosion, and photograph hotspots. Monitor assets and infrastructure within the zone of influence.
- Record inspections, erosion warning indicator can be found on: https://mapshare.vic.gov.au/coastkit/
- Check coastal hazard warning:
https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
https://www.emergency.vic.gov.au/respond/#
Mitigation:
- Continue T1 and T2 controls. Apply permeating grouting as a priority at hotspots threatening assets. Add extra silt fence or blanket coverage along the full affected waterfront. Install temporary protection for threatened assets. Stop works that disturb the area until stabilised.
- Immediate repair of any failed control. No work continues in the area until controls are restored.
- Monitor receiving water during and after all works. Stop discharge or grouting that causes an exceedance, and escalate.
Communication:
- Notify the Construction Manager immediately. The Construction Manager decides on stop-work. A geotechnical or coastal engineer assesses the hotspot and approves the design for grouting or protection works.

column8:

- Continue work. Stop or reschedule any activity that the existing controls cannot mitigate.
- Check high wind warning: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
https://www.emergency.vic.gov.au/respond/#
Mitigation:
- Secure loose materials and temporary building components. Check bracing and anchoring of exposed structures.
- Apply water or dust suppression to exposed areas. Cover loads and stockpiles.
Communication:

column9:

- Check high wind warning: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
https://www.emergency.vic.gov.au/respond/#
Mitigation:
- Stop high-risk activities when wind exceeds safe limits. Reprogram dust-generating work (e.g. soil screening, crushing, cut and fill). Cease any dust activity that cannot be controlled.
- Inspect connections and temporary bracing. Strengthen or protect vulnerable roof and facade elements. Secure all materials and waste, and tie down covers.
- Increase water spraying, apply soil binders to unstable areas, and stabilise disturbed areas.
Communication:
- Notify the PIC and Construction Manager. The Construction Manager approves any continued work.
column10:

- Check high wind warning: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
https://www.emergency.vic.gov.au/respond/#
Mitigation:
- Stop all work. Move people to shelter. Keep everyone clear of exposed structures, scaffolds and hoisted loads.
- Secure incomplete structures with temporary bracing and supports until stable. Make safe any failed or loosened component before anyone approaches it.
- Stop haulage and all dust-generating work. Stabilise exposed areas where it is safe to do so. Record any off-site dust impact or complaint.
Communication:
- Notify the Construction Manager immediately. Call 000 for any injury. Report events under the project event management procedure.

column9:

Mitigation:
Limit ignition-risk work (hot work, grinding, welding) to low-risk times, or defer it. Decide in advance whether to stay or leave if conditions worsen, and when. Park vehicles facing the exit. Put the Emergency Response Team on standby. Confirm the evacuation routes and the grass-free muster point are clear. Monitor VicEmergency continuously.

- Fire wardens:
Activate the “Evacuate” alarm. Confirm the office and amenities are cleared. Close all doors and windows when checking offices. Account for evacuated personnel.
- HSE staff:

column3:
No sign of coastal erosion.
Investigation hazard:
Area below 10 m contour within 1000 m from the coast in non-Lidar mapper areas
column4:
Low hazard:
- Shoreline recession due to SLR in 2100
- Fresh scarping, undercutting or vegetation loss, or new cracks near the shoreline during routine inspection.
- Area at risk of inundation from a 1-in-100 year storm event in 2100
column5:
Medium hazard:
- The area is at risk of inundation from 1-in-100 year storm event in 2050
- Area at risk from shoreline recession due to SLR in 2050 & storm bite erosion from 1 in 100 year storm
- Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) watch or advice for the area. Forecast high tide plus storm surge or large swell.
- Measured retreat above a set distance since the last survey or after a storm. Controls or assets within a set distance of the scarp edge.
column6:
High hazard:
- The area is at risk from a mean high tide in 2050
- Area is currently at risk from storm bite erosion from 1 in 100 year storm
- BoM flood or severe weather warning for the area. Forecast or observed water level approaching the work area or asset.
- Water over the work area, access roads or assets, or an emergency warning issued.
- Rapid retreat during an event, or a hotspot threatening an asset or infrastructure.
column7:
Monitor:
Get a site-specific assessment by a qualified coastal engineer. Set baseline survey points and photo points. Check BoM and tide forecasts.
Mitigation:
Stock silt fence and erosion control blanket on site.
Identify the lowest-lying work areas, access roads and assets. Mark the flood-prone areas on the site plan. Stock sandbags, pumps, barriers and temporary lighting.
Escalation:
Record the baseline and the hazard band for each work area.
column8:

- Check coastal warning alert: https://alert.tas.gov.au/?view=both
- Check coastal weather warning: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
Mitigation:
- Place erosion control blanket on disturbed or open sediment on the waterfront. Install silt fence to hold coarse sediment while letting water through.
- Check that drains, culverts and stormwater pits are clear. Confirm the pumps work. Review where plant, materials and fuel are stored.
Escalation:
The supervisor records the trigger and briefs the crew.
column9:
Monitor:
- Inspect daily and before and after every storm or high tide. Resurvey against the baseline.
- Check coastal warning alert: https://alert.tas.gov.au/?view=both
- Check coastal weather warning: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
Mitigation:
- Extend blanket and silt fence to all active erosion areas. Apply permeating grouting to areas showing active erosion.
- Raise or move plant, materials, fuel and chemicals to higher ground. Place sandbags or temporary barriers at low points and around key assets. Set up pumps. Secure loose items and temporary works. Plan the evacuation route and check that it stays above water.
Escalation:
Notify the PIC and Construction Manager. Review the work plan and move plant, materials and people back from the edge.
column10:
Monitor:
- Continuous monitoring by the supervisor. Survey retreat during and after the event. Track water levels and warnings.
- Check coastal warning alert: https://alert.tas.gov.au/?view=both
- Check fire weather warning: https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts
Mitigation:
- Apply permeating grouting as a priority at hotspots near assets. Add silt fence and blanket along the full affected waterfront. Stop works that disturb the area until stabilised.
- Stop work in flood-prone areas and evacuate people to higher ground. Isolate power and shut off fuel and gas. Secure or remove anything that could float or wash away. Close access roads under water. Do not enter floodwater.
Escalation:
Notify the Construction Manager immediately. Stop work in the area, evacuate if water approaches, and call 000 for any emergency. A coastal engineer assesses before work resumes.

height

https://alert.tas.gov.au/?view=both
https://www.bom.gov.au/marine/wind.shtml?unit=p0&location=tas&tz=AEDT

https://alert.tas.gov.au/?view=both
https://www.bom.gov.au/marine/wind.shtml?unit=p0&location=tas&tz=AEDT

- Secure materials and equipment; inspect structural connections and temporary supports.

https://www.bom.gov.au/marine/wind.shtml?unit=p0&location=tas&tz=AEDT

Mitigation:

- Isolate affected areas and restrict access
